result.summary:
KOD lab (kod-machine/) is a forensic ledger, not a scanner: a case = a hashed card (symbol, venue, call_type, decision_cutoff, three information sets at exactly T-30D/T-72H/T-24H, story, disposition, critic, frozen KOD-DET-v0 evaluations) anchored in git with RFC 3161 tokens; outcomes are a later append-only row. RETROSPECTIVE cards reconstruct past moves and never count; PROSPECTIVE cards must be STRICT-v3 (every non-null fact cites a recorded KOD-EVIDENCE-v2 object published by that set's cutoff, grade A-C, recorded before the open), opened within 1 hour of decision_cutoff and before a pre-registered outcome_window.start, with at least one TSA answering and the anchor commit pushed; they count only when AUTHORITATIVE (GitHub push-run receipt for the exact anchor commit dated before window start). Scoring: per-detector hit rate on both sides over AUTHORITATIVE closed prospective cases, hit = REPRICED_UP for four detectors, REPRICED_DOWN for NARRATIVE_WITHOUT_MECHANISM; calibration NOT_STARTED until 30 such cases; detector_table is always UNVALIDATED/promotable=false.
Current state (var/kod.db, read-only): 4 cases (NVDA, SMCI retrospective v1; ZEAL retrospective v3 PARTIAL; one SIMULATED), 0 prospective, 0 scans, 19 evidence objects (all ZEALAND: 15 B, 2 C, 2 D), 0 GitHub receipts, 96 tests. Detector source still hashes to the bound value (0a0e0a73...), doctrine 246deb4a..., so an open today is not refused on those grounds.
What an open today needs: evidence declarations recorded first (kod evidence, each needs source_url/type/publisher/document_type/publication_time+basis/retrieval_time/as_of_cutoff/grade/existence_method/content_method/provenance; bytes optional), a card from seeds/prospective_template.json with decision_cutoff = the run minute, set cutoffs exactly -30d/-72h/-24h, a future window, a critic note, disposition WATCH/REJECT (INVESTIGATE needs the critic), network to freetsa/sectigo, git push of the anchor commit, then GITHUB_TOKEN for `kod receipt fetch`, and commit var/kod.db. Nothing in code chooses the name: the card is operator-authored; the only machine link is scan_entry_id to a `kod scan` logged earlier with every name evaluated. Close = after window end, with card_sha and an operator-supplied outcome_label from {REPRICED_UP, REPRICED_DOWN, NO_REPRICE, UNKNOWN, CENSORED}; KOD codes no % threshold, so the outcome rule must be pre-registered in the card text.
Feed analysis: the idxsig paper scan (US 22:53Z after a 20:00Z close, 15 G2_RET30 candidates on 2026-10-13; crypto 00:25Z; IDX 10:26Z) fits KOD's timing gate (open within the hour, window = next session onward). But KOD's structure puts the +30% day outside every information set if the card is opened the same evening (T-24H ends before that session), so the detectors evaluate pre-spike facts and the spike is T-0 context in story text only; if instead the card is opened the next evening so T-24H includes the spike, PRIMARY_DOC_BEFORE_PRICE and VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET are NO_SIGNAL by construction (they require price not repriced / quiet) and the window skips d+1, where E2 found the median lead to peak is 1 session. The well-formed prospective ask is "does it reprice again (+30% from the signal close) within d+1..d+5", which matches the paper ledger's own E30 scoring and has historical reference only (E2 validation 2023: P(E30|G2) US 15.4%, crypto 18.5%; median 5-session return after a flag -10.3% / -11.5%). "Does a catalyst surface" is not a KOD outcome label (schema CHECK), only a T-24H input fact; a catalyst appearing after the open cannot be scored without a new migration and doctrine version. Doctrine 79-81 forbids a winner list without non-events, so the legitimate KOD-shaped integration is `kod scan` of the whole scanned universe (flagged = G2_RET30, facts optional, no evidence burden), which yields the FLAG:G2_RET30 lift row against a prospective base rate; opening 15 STRICT cases/day is infeasible on evidence throughput (ZEALAND took 19 objects for one name). A pre-repricing watchlist is needed to test the detectors as designed; its non-outcome-selected sources are dated-catalyst calendars (DATED_CATALYST_KNOWN), primary-document feeds such as EDGAR/IDX disclosures (PRIMARY_DOC_BEFORE_PRICE, NARRATIVE_WITHOUT_MECHANISM) and a tape pre-screen from the bars the paper scan already pulls, using the ZEALAND protocol's fact definitions frozen 2026-10-08 (ret20>=30%, 5v20 volume ratio>=1.5, rngr<=1 and |ret5|<=2*vol20*sqrt5) rather than new thresholds; each would be a new scanner id logged via `kod scan`, not an edit to KOD-DET-v0.

Timing arithmetic for a same-evening US case: open at 23:00Z on day d gives T-24H cutoff 23:00Z on d-1 (before session d), T-72H 23:00Z on d-3, T-30D 23:00Z on d-30; session d's +30% bar is therefore outside every information set; opening at 23:00Z on d+1 puts session d inside T-24H but forces outcome_window.start after the d+1 session has already traded (check_prospective_timing: now < start).
constraints: Prospective open must be STRICT-v3: every non-null fact in all three sets cites KOD-EVIDENCE-v2 objects recorded before the open, published by that set's cutoff, as_of_cutoff <= set cutoff, grade A-C only (kod/evidence.py:217-281; kod/ledger.py:444-449, 472-474).

decision_cutoff within 1 hour of the actual open; outcome_window.start after both; set cutoffs exactly decision_cutoff - 30d / -72h / -24h with timezone (kod/ledger.py:33-41, 174-217; kod/hashing.py:22-29).

A prospective open or scan is refused and rolled back if no RFC 3161 authority answers (kod/anchor.py:135-137; kod/ledger.py:563, 704) and if no git anchor/registry is configured (ledger.py:463-464, 615-616).

Only AUTHORITATIVE cases count: anchor commit pushed, GitHub push-run receipt for exactly that commit created before outcome_window.start, re-checked live with GITHUB_TOKEN (kod/verify.py:9-12, 96-133; kod/remote.py:122-160); receipts expire after ~410 days (kod-machine/README.md:168-174).

kod/detectors.py may not change while RULE_VERSION stays KOD-DET-v0; a changed detector or hit label is a new rule version and a new cohort (detectors.py:3, 19-23; ledger.py:333-341; verify.py:221-224). Doctrine 62-66: thresholds cannot be edited in place.

Doctrine 43-51: retrospective and simulated rows never count toward calibration; doctrine 79-81 and README 274-275: a scanner feed must log every name evaluated, flagged or not, or there is no base rate.

Outcome labels are the schema enum only (schema.sql:72-74, migrations/002_hardening.sql:68-70); 'a catalyst surfaced' is not an outcome; adding one needs a new migration and a new doctrine version (doctrine 56-58; schema.sql:1-2).
Close only after outcome_window.end with the card_sha printed at open; one outcome per case; rows are append-only by trigger (ledger.py:576-609; schema.sql:80-150; migrations 002-004 triggers).
Detector evaluations must carry recorded_at == opened_at (migrations/003:37-43) and are inside the card hash (ledger.py:134-139, 501-503), so facts cannot be revised after the open.
Doctrine 30-41: a fact is storable only if public at or before the horizon cutoff; NEWLY_FOUND_OLD cannot support a prospective call; missing is UNKNOWN (null), never false.

Standing rules: IDX holdout 2024-01-02..2025-02-21 and US/crypto 2024 onward are sealed (backtest.py:78-80; research/E2/PROTOCOL.md:16); no re-tuning of frozen detectors on seen outcomes; no orders; read-only this session.
Registry files are append-only under tools/check_append_only.py and the pre-commit hook; registry line edits refuse new anchors (anchor.py:127-128).
gaps: No prospective case has ever been opened; the full chain (real TSA stamp + push + `kod receipt fetch` against live GitHub + AUTHORITATIVE in `kod report`) has only run with FakeTimestamper/FakeGitHub in tests. remote_timestamp_receipts is empty.

KOD codes no repricing threshold: REPRICED_UP/DOWN/NO_REPRICE are operator text at close. A post-spike or pre-spike protocol must pre-register the rule (e.g. +30% from the signal close within 5 sessions, per paper.py:540) in the card and critic text before the first open; whether window_return_pct should be close-to-close, max-close, or home-listing official close is undefined in kod/.

Doctrine line 65 requires 'complete coverage' for promotion; score.py does not check it, and COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE fires on every PARTIAL_PUBLIC card (all four existing cases). How a prospective US/crypto case reaches anything other than PARTIAL_PUBLIC is undefined.

Evidence throughput is unknown for a daily feed: ZEALAND took 19 objects for one name over one afternoon; 15 US candidates/day x 3 sets x up to 8 facts at STRICT is untested. Whether EDGAR acceptance timestamps (PRIMARY_SOURCE_TIMESTAMP, grade B) and RFC 3161-stamped Yahoo bar captures (SECONDARY, EXTERNAL_TIMESTAMP_RECEIPT, grade B ceiling) are acceptable price/document evidence prospectively has not been decided or tried.

`kod scan` at paper-scan scale (5,600 US names, every entry hashed into registry/scans/<id>.json and anchored per run) is untested; tests use a handful of entries. Closing 5,600 scan outcomes per scan after the window has no tooling (scan-close takes a hand-built outcomes JSON).

The paper scan's features.csv lacks vol20 and rngr, so the ZEALAND price-fact definitions (price_quiet_vs_own_range, volume_creep 5v20) would need recomputation from the manifest-logged bars; no code does this.

Whether this environment can reach freetsa.org / timestamp.sectigo.com and push to origin right now is unknown (last success 2026-10-08T12:44Z for the ZEAL open; the paper routines push daily through 2026-10-14T00:27Z).

No pre-repricing watchlist source exists in the repo: no catalyst calendar, no EDGAR/IDX disclosure feed, no pre-spike tape screen; E1/E2's 'prior volatility' finding (AUC 0.68 IDX, 0.78 US) is on seen data and is hypothesis-only.
E4 (PR #7) results on the branch were not read; whether its crypto validation passed is unknown here and should not be assumed.

Unknown: who the human operator for daily evidence declarations and critic notes would be, and whether the operator clock discipline (open within the hour, close only after window end, commit kod.db) can be met by a scheduled routine.
